Equipped with higher voltages, we can return to using trusty VHB 3910 and still create movement on a usable scale.

Two final set-ups of EAPs have been built. The first set-up follows the “drum” design as seen in Figures 3 and 4, while the other set-up has a vertical configuration in order to facilitate the addition of load.

The load-bearing EAP apparatus is comprised of a series of 0.4 inch spaced vertically drilled holes in an aluminum base. Two aluminum dowels are then inserted into these holes to create two vertical poles. One of these dowels is fixed in its hole at one end of the base while the other dowel remains unattached to the base (free to rotate or be moved to other holes). VHB 3910 is then stretched between the plates and fixed by wrapping the adhesive polymer around the dowels and back onto itself. Greased active areas, trails, and copper ribbon are also added in the same way as the “drum” set-up. The only missing part now becomes the application of load. After much thought as to how to incorporate such a feature without damaging the EAP, the final result involved a washer tied to a fine string that is attached just below the active area of the VHB using “plastix” glue (Fig. 6). The washer serves as a 1.5 gram load and can also be used to affix larger loads by incorporating a nut and bolt for example. Video of actuated EAPs can be found at othello.mech.nwu.edu/~peshkin/eap.⁷
